transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… mostly I came in because I’m just not sleeping right anymore. Like I’ll lie there for hours, and if it’s raining I start listening to it too much, or I get thinking about the bluff giving way, and then my brain just won’t shut up.

And then when I finally do pass out, I wake up all sweaty from dreams, and I’ve gotta go to the call center the next day feeling like I didn’t sleep at all. Which is bad because people on the phone already get mad over little stuff, and I’m just sitting there trying to sound normal. So… yeah, the sleep thing is kind of why I’m here.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you once found pleasurable?

I don’t know… I mean, I guess I haven’t really been keeping track like that. I still do stuff sometimes, but it’s more like after work I’m just tired and I end up messing around on my phone or whatever.

Like, I used to go over to my cousin’s place sometimes, he’s got this old game console that barely works unless you hit the side of it—sorry, that’s not really what you asked. I guess I’m not sure if I’m enjoying things less, or if I just don’t have the energy to think about it much.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about things, even when there isn’t a clear reason, or feel like your anxiety is hard to control?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if it’s “worrying” exactly. It’s more like there’s this feeling under everything most days, like I’m scared for no reason, or embarrassed, like people can tell I screwed something up.

Even at work, someone will just ask me a normal question and I’ll be thinking, like, do they notice I’m not… I don’t know, as tough as I used to try to act? Which sounds dumb when I say it. It’s not always about one clear thing, it just kind of sits there.
Do you find yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself for things, even when other people wouldn’t see them as that big of a deal?

Yeah… I do, I guess. I keep going back over it like, why was I even out there by myself? Like I should’ve known better, or I was being stupid or careless or something.

And then it kind of spreads out past that, if that makes sense. Like now even in regular places, I feel like if I relax for one second, something bad’s gonna happen. Which… I don’t know, other people probably wouldn’t think about it that way. But it’s hard not to.
Do you find that these feelings of fear or guilt are almost always there, even when you’re not in a stressful situation or thinking about something specific?

Yeah… most days it’s kind of just there. Not always loud, I guess, but underneath everything.

Like even if nothing’s happening, I’ll be at work or just standing in line somewhere and I feel scared or embarrassed, like everybody can tell I messed up somehow. Or like they can see I’m not as tough as I used to act, which… I know people probably aren’t thinking about me that much. But it still feels that way.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms like muscle tension, restlessness, or being easily startled, even when you're not actively worried about something?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I don’t sit there and think, like, “my muscles are tense” or whatever. Sometimes I don’t notice my body until somebody points it out, you know?

Like at work I’m usually just trying to get through the next customer, and then I’ll realize I’ve been standing weird or I haven’t moved in a while—but I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean. The being startled thing… I don’t know. I’d have to think about it. I don’t really keep track of that stuff.
Do you often feel tense or like your muscles are tight, even when you're not particularly worried or stressed about something?

I don’t know if I’d say often. I mean… I get stiff sometimes, but I also stand at a counter a lot, so maybe that’s just from work, you know? Like my shoulders or my back will feel weird and then I’m thinking about whether I lifted something wrong or slept bad.

I don’t really pay attention until later. If I’m not stressed, I’m usually just trying to do whatever I’m doing, and then I notice after. So… I’m not sure if it’s tension like you mean.
Do you notice any physical symptoms like a racing heart, stomach upset, or dizziness that happen even when you're not particularly stressed or worried?

I don’t really know. Like, I’ve had my heart beat fast before, but I don’t know if that’s just from running around at work or drinking too much coffee or whatever.

Stomach stuff… I mean, everybody gets that sometimes, right? I don’t really connect it to anything. I guess I don’t pay close enough attention to say it happens when I’m not stressed. Dizziness, not really that I’ve noticed. I’d probably just think I didn’t eat or something.
Can you recall times when your body felt tense or your heart raced even when you weren't stressed or busy, like when you're just sitting quietly at home?

I’m trying to think of, like, just sitting on the couch or something… I don’t know. I don’t really notice that stuff unless it gets in the way.

Usually if my heart’s going fast I figure there’s a reason, like I had coffee or I was moving around. At home I’m usually watching videos or just kind of zoning out, and I don’t sit there checking my body. So… I can’t really say I remember a time like that, no.
Have you found yourself being extra watchful or on guard, like something bad might happen again, especially since the event you mentioned earlier?

Yeah… I mean, I guess I am. I don’t always think of it like “on guard,” but I catch myself looking around more, checking who’s nearby, where I’m standing, stuff like that.

And it’s like… I keep going back to thinking I was stupid for being out there alone. Like I should’ve known better, or I was just careless. So now if I’m anywhere and I’m not paying attention, it feels like that’s when something bad is gonna happen. I know that probably sounds kind of dramatic, but that’s how it feels.
Do you find yourself thinking about the event when you don’t want to, or having memories of it come up even when you’re trying not to think about it?

Yeah… yeah, that happens. Not like I’m sitting there trying to think about it, it just kind of pops in.

Like I’ll be at my desk with the headset on, trying to deal with some customer complaining about their bill or whatever, and all of a sudden I’ll hear in my head that sound of rocks sliding. Or I’ll get this picture of my leg stuck under me, and for a second it’s like I’m not even at work, I’m back on that trail.

And then I’ll kind of snap out of it and realize I missed what the person was saying, which is embarrassing. I don’t know why it comes up right then. It’s not like I’m trying to bring it up.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities because they remind you of what happened?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t go near those coast trails anymore. Like, even if someone just mentions hiking out there, I kind of shut down.

My old hiking buddies still text sometimes, like “we should go this weekend,” or they send pictures of places, and I’ll just not answer. Which is kind of messed up because they’re not doing anything wrong. But even talking about going back out there, my chest gets tight and I start thinking, like, no, I can’t do that. So I just avoid the whole thing.
Do you find yourself feeling afraid, guilty, or ashamed even when you’re not thinking about what happened on the trail?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not always like I’m actively thinking about the trail, you know? Sometimes I’m just at work or walking into a store or whatever, and there’s this feeling underneath everything.

Like I feel scared, but also embarrassed, I guess. Like people can look at me and tell I messed up somehow. Which is stupid because nobody at the grocery store knows anything about me, they’re just buying chips or whatever… but I still feel like I’m not as tough as I used to act. Like before I would’ve said I could handle stuff, and now I don’t feel that way most days.

inference_history.note: This turn added more evidence for disorders related to anxiety and trauma, specifically highlighting symptoms of persistent guilt, intrusive thoughts, and hypervigilance. This makes F43.12 (Generalized Anxiety Disorder) and F43.22 (Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder) the most likely diagnoses. F32.2 (Major Depressive Disorder, Severe) and F41.1 (Panic Disorder) are ruled out due to lack of evidence for full-criteria depressive episodes or recurrent panic attacks.

The patient reports persistent feelings of fear and guilt even in non-stressful situations, which broadens the differential to include Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1), but the symptoms also align with Major Depressive Disorder (F43.22) and Adjustment Disorder with Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood (F43.23). However, based on prior candidates and the chronic underlying emotional distress, F43.12 (Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder) remains relevant, and F43.22 is still plausible due to overlapping symptoms. F43.02 (Adjustment Disorder with Anxiety) is considered due to the subthreshold nature of symptoms and possible stress-related onset).

The patient has reported symptoms of persistent fear, intrusive memories of a traumatic event, avoidance of reminders, and hypervigilance. These findings support the possibility of PTSD (F43.12). The previous candidate F43.02 (Acute Stress Reaction) is ruled out as the symptoms have persisted beyond one month and are not limited to an immediate reaction to the trauma. Further evaluation is needed to confirm PTSD or rule out other anxiety disorders.
